_comment: Golden fixture for post-mortem producer saved_dollars math (reporting.py:50-71). The bug: when triggered_basket_snapshot is non-empty and live_prices are provided, post_trigger_move collapses to ~0 (basket prices pinned near exit), so live_ret ≈ f_ret → near-zero saved. The correct if-held source is shadow_history.current_return, which the engine records accurately. All expected values are DERIVED from the fixture inputs — never hardcoded from producer output.

cases.name: basket_prices_stale_current_return_diverges
cases.description: Bot locked in at +1.85%. If-held (shadow_history.current_return) is +0.63% — a 1.22pp divergence on a $1020 position ($12.44 saved). The basket reconstruction collapses to near exit return because ticker prices barely moved from the trigger price (simulating the stale/at-exit basket bug). The CORRECT producer must use current_return, NOT the basket reconstruction.

cases.name: large_divergence_basket_near_exit_current_return_negative
cases.description: Bot exited at +2.82%. If-held fell to +0.37% (shadow_history.current_return). Divergence = 2.45pp on $985 = $24.13. Basket prices barely moved from snapshot → basket reconstruction ≈ exit return ≈ $0 saved (the bug). Correct producer uses current_return.

cases.name: current_return_above_exit_negative_guard_alpha
cases.description: Bot exited at +0.67%. If-held actually recovered to +1.15% (shadow_history.current_return). Guard alpha is negative (market recovered past exit). Saved = (0.67 - 1.15)/100 * $1200 = -$5.76. Basket reconstruction again gives near-zero (bug path), hiding the real negative outcome.
